title: Four-eigenvalue sign-imbalance reduction and hub obstruction

results.name: sign-imbalanced four-eigenvalue chamber
results.statement: If s4(A)>=s and among the eigenvalues with absolute value at least s there are three of the same sign, then the density of X^T A X+b^T X+c is at most 270 K^2/s.
normalized_proof: Pivot branches already close under s4>=1: a scalar pivot leaves at least three unit-scale Schur directions and uses the proved s3 half-moment theorem; definite pair is direct; indefinite pair leaves at least two Schur directions, while the concentration lemma only needs nonzero operator norm.
In the no-pivot chamber choose three orthonormal eigenvectors Phi with eigenvalues Lambda all >=1, after replacing A by -A if necessary.
The Section 6 sign argument with k=3 gives a physical cut and C=(A-DAD)/2 such that 2 Phi^T C Phi = Lambda-Phi^T diag(A) Phi-Q and ||Q||<=sqrt(2)*(5/48)*3.
By min-max, C has three positive eigenvalues above this number. Since C is the symmetric dilation of A_IJ, s3(A_IJ)>0.2373624642.
Therefore E3(A_IJ)>gamma^6 and Corollary 4.3(a) gives density < C3/gamma = 62.4292 in the no-pivot branch. The pivot maximum is below 270. Standard K,s scaling finishes.
results.downstream: The only genuinely new s4 signature after this reduction is balanced 2-positive/2-negative at the threshold.

results.name: five-way balanced-s4 router
results.statement: The account01/B06 router is algebraically sound: for normalized s4>=1, at least one of diagonal pivot, principal-pair pivot, s5>=1e-3, order-3 physical crossing >=1e-3, or a literal two-hub pair H with small A_HH and lambda_min(A_HR A_HR^T)>9e-5 occurs.
checks: The heavy/light sign split has E||Z||_F^2<delta and gives the claimed lower bounds on lambda_min(Phi_I^T Phi_I) and lambda_3(Phi_J^T Phi_J).
The singular-value product lower bound for the rank-four spectral core is valid.
Cauchy-Binet converts kappa2 mass to a physical heavy pair; G=(A^2)_HH-A_HH^2 and A^2>=Phi Phi^T yield the stated Gram lower bound.
results.downstream: Branches 1-4 are already paid by the five-eigenvalue paper. The exact A_HH=0 endpoint of branch 5 is paid by the sharp zero-two-hub theorem. The first unpaid s4 endpoint is therefore balanced signature with a small nonzero 2x2 literal hub block.

results.name: small nonzero hub block plus strong hub Gram is insufficient without the fourth-direction currency
results.construction: Let B=diag(eps,-eps), C=I2, D=C^T B^{-1} C=diag(1/eps,-1/eps), and take four independent centered uniform coordinates U1,U2,Y1,Y2. Then Q=eps(U1+Y1/eps)^2-eps(U2-Y2/eps)^2.
properties: A_HH=B can be arbitrarily small and A_HR A_HR^T=I2.
The two squared factors are independent and each square has an inverse-square-root singularity at zero, so their difference has a logarithmically unbounded density at zero.
The full block matrix has Schur complement zero and rank two, so this is not an s4 counterexample.
results.downstream: Any nonzero-hub receiver used in the balanced s4 branch must spend the two surviving Schur/spectral directions; a bound depending only on small ||A_HH|| and det(A_HR A_HR^T) is false.

open_obligation: Construct a product-preserving receiver for the balanced 2+2 branch with two literal hubs, lambda_min(A_HR A_HR^T)>9e-5 and small nonzero A_HH, explicitly using the two Schur directions. Do not scalarize or discard the hub block. Full s4 and unrestricted s3 density remain OPEN.
